claim: The anterior insular cortex (AIC) mediates interoceptive attention which refers to attention towards physiological signals arising from the body.
source: Accumulating evidence indicates that the anterior insular cortex (AIC) mediates interoceptive attention which refers to attention towards physiological signals arising from the body.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature and is stated as an established finding in the field.

claim: The necessity of the AIC in interoceptive attention has not been demonstrated prior to this study.
source: However, the necessity of the AIC in this process has not been demonstrated.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the literature prior to the current study.

claim: Interoceptive attention was associated with increased AIC activation.
source: Results showed that interoceptive attention was associated with increased AIC activation, as well as enhanced coupling between the AIC and somatosensory areas along with reduced coupling between the AIC and visual sensory areas.
evidence: This claim is supported by the fMRI experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Interoceptive attention was associated with enhanced coupling between the AIC and somatosensory areas.
source: Results showed that interoceptive attention was associated with increased AIC activation, as well as enhanced coupling between the AIC and somatosensory areas along with reduced coupling between the AIC and visual sensory areas.
evidence: This claim is supported by connectivity analysis (PPI and DCM) of fMRI data.

claim: Interoceptive attention was associated with reduced coupling between the AIC and visual sensory areas.
source: Results showed that interoceptive attention was associated with increased AIC activation, as well as enhanced coupling between the AIC and somatosensory areas along with reduced coupling between the AIC and visual sensory areas.
evidence: This claim is supported by connectivity analysis (PPI and DCM) of fMRI data.

claim: AIC activation was predictive of individual differences in interoceptive accuracy.
source: In addition, AIC activation was predictive of individual differences in interoceptive accuracy.
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis between AIC activation and behavioral performance.

claim: AIC lesion patients showed disrupted interoceptive discrimination accuracy and sensitivity.
source: Importantly, AIC lesion patients showed disrupted interoceptive discrimination accuracy and sensitivity.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data from the lesion study comparing AIC patients to controls.

claim: The AIC plays a critical role in interoceptive attention.
source: These results provide compelling evidence that the AIC plays a critical role in interoceptive attention.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the combined fMRI and lesion study data.

claim: Subjective emotions arise from bodily reactions and visceral experiences.
source: Previous theories argue that subjective emotions arise from these bodily reactions and visceral experiences (Cannon, 1987; Critchley and Harrison, 2013; Damasio, 1996; Dolan, 2002; Tranel and Damasio, 1991) in which interoceptive awareness plays a critical role.
evidence: This claim is attributed to previous theoretical work cited in the manuscript.

claim: Interoceptive awareness plays a critical role in subjective emotions arising from bodily reactions.
source: Previous theories argue that subjective emotions arise from these bodily reactions and visceral experiences (Cannon, 1987; Critchley and Harrison, 2013; Damasio, 1996; Dolan, 2002; Tranel and Damasio, 1991) in which interoceptive awareness plays a critical role.
evidence: This claim is attributed to previous theoretical work cited in the manuscript.

claim: Appropriate attention to bodily states and accurate perception of interoceptive information are essential in emotional awareness.
source: Appropriate attention to bodily states and accurate perception of interoceptive information are essential in emotional awareness and in the maintenance of normal physiological conditions (Craig, 2002; Craig, 2003; Craig, 2010; Critchley, 2005; Wiens, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Appropriate attention to bodily states and accurate perception of interoceptive information are essential in the maintenance of normal physiological conditions.
source: Appropriate attention to bodily states and accurate perception of interoceptive information are essential in emotional awareness and in the maintenance of normal physiological conditions (Craig, 2002; Craig, 2003; Craig, 2010; Critchley, 2005; Wiens, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The AIC is an important structure for encoding and representing interoceptive information.
source: Neuroanatomical evidence, consistent with neuroimaging findings, suggests that the anterior insular cortex (AIC) is an important structure for encoding and representing interoceptive information (Craig, 2002; Craig, 2003; Craig, 2009; Critchley et al., 2004; Stephani et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to neuroanatomical and neuroimaging studies.

claim: AIC activation seems ubiquitous across a wide range of tasks involving cognition, emotion, and other cognitive processes in addition to interoceptive attention.
source: Although the AIC has been recognized as an interoceptive cortex (Craig, 2003; Critchley et al., 2004; Ernst et al., 2014; Singer et al., 2009; Terasawa et al., 2013), these findings remain equivocal because AIC activation seems ubiquitous across a wide range of tasks involving cognition, emotion, and other cognitive processes in addition to interoceptive attention (Allen et al., 2013; Seeley et al., 2007; Uddin et al., 2014; Yarkoni et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous neuroimaging studies showing widespread AIC activation.

claim: Correlational AIC activation found in functional neuroimaging studies alone does not provide causal evidence for its role in interoceptive attention.
source: In addition, the correlational AIC activation found in functional neuroimaging studies alone does not provide causal evidence for its role in interoceptive attention, leaving the question of whether the AIC is critical in interoceptive attention unanswered.
evidence: This is a methodological statement about the limitations of correlational neuroimaging evidence.

claim: Studying patients with focal lesions in the AIC would provide a unique opportunity to examine the necessity of the AIC in interoceptive attention.
source: Studying patients with focal lesions in the AIC (Gu et al., 2012; Gu et al., 2015; Ronchi et al., 2015; Starr et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2019) would thus provide a unique opportunity to examine the necessity of the AIC in this fundamental process.
evidence: This is a methodological rationale supported by citations to previous lesion studies.

claim: Most existing tasks measuring interoceptive attention fail to meet the criterion that only contents that are clearly perceived and represented by the mind can be the target of attention.
source: According to the classic definition of attention by James (1890), only the contents that are clearly perceived and represented by the mind can be the target of attention. However, most existing tasks measuring interoceptive attention fail to meet this criterion (Ring et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a review of interoceptive attention tasks.

claim: Precise measurements of interoceptive attention are difficult to obtain experimentally because of the imprecise perception of visceral changes, such as heart rate.
source: In contrast to exteroceptive attention toward external sensory inputs, precise measurements of interoceptive attention are difficult to obtain experimentally because of the imprecise perception of visceral changes, such as heart rate (Brener and Ring, 2016; Paulus and Stein, 2010; Ring et al., 2015; Windmann et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous methodological discussions.

claim: Breathing is an essential activity for maintaining human life.
source: Breathing is an essential activity for maintaining human life and, more importantly, is an easily perceivable bodily signal.
evidence: This is a statement of general biological knowledge.

claim: Breathing is an easily perceivable bodily signal.
source: Breathing is an essential activity for maintaining human life and, more importantly, is an easily perceivable bodily signal.
evidence: This is a statement based on common experience and physiological knowledge.

claim: Breathing can be measured and actively controlled in humans.
source: As an autonomous vital movement, breathing can be measured and actively controlled in humans (Daubenmier et al., 2013; Davenport et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The unique physiological characteristics of respiration render breath detection an ideal method for measuring interoceptive accuracy and sensitivity.
source: The unique physiological characteristics of respiration render breath detection an ideal method for measuring interoceptive accuracy and sensitivity (Garfinkel et al., 2015) and for exploring the neural activity underlying interoceptive attention.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and represents a methodological rationale.

claim: The AIC is critical for interoceptive attention to reach subjective awareness by integrating information from an individual's homeostatic state and the external environment.
source: Basing from previous evidence (e.g., Critchley, 2004), we hypothesized that the AIC is critical for interoceptive attention to reach subjective awareness by integrating information from an individual's homeostatic state and the external environment.
evidence: This is the stated hypothesis of the study, based on previous evidence.

claim: The main effect of interoceptive attention (BDT vs. DDT) was associated with enhanced activity in the cognitive control network, including the AIC, the dorsal ACC, the SMA, and the superior frontal and parietal cortices.
source: The main effect of interoceptive attention, compared to exteroceptive attention (BDT vs. DDT), was associated with enhanced activity in the cognitive control network (Fan, 2014; Wu et al., 2015; Xuan et al., 2016), including the AIC, the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and the supplementary motor area (SMA), and the superior frontal and the parietal cortices (the frontal eye field, FEF; and the areas near/along the intraparietal sulcus; Figure 2a, Table 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by whole brain fMRI analysis results shown in Figure 2a and Table 3.

claim: The main effect of interoceptive attention revealed significantly less activation (deactivation) in core regions of the default mode network, including the ventral medial prefrontal cortex, the MTG, and the posterior cingulate cortex.
source: In addition, this contrast revealed significantly less activation, or deactivation, in the core regions of the default mode network (Raichle et al., 2001), including the the ventral medial prefrontal cortex, the middle temporal gyrus (MTG), and the posterior cingulate cortex.
evidence: This claim is supported by whole brain fMRI analysis results.

claim: Activation in the AIC, the middle frontal gyrus, the SMA, and the temporal parietal junction was associated with the main effect of feedback delay.
source: Activation in the AIC, the middle frontal gyrus, the SMA, and the temporal parietal junction was associated with the main effect of feedback delay (Figure 2b, Table 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by whole brain fMRI analysis results shown in Figure 2b and Table 4.

claim: Regions showing the main effect of feedback delay also showed the interaction effect between attentional focus and feedback.
source: The regions showing the main effect of feedback delay also showed the interaction effect between attentional focus (interoceptively in the BDT and exteroceptively in the DDT) and feedback (with and without delay) (Figure 2c, Table 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by whole brain fMRI analysis results shown in Figure 2c and Table 5.

claim: The bilateral AIC demonstrated greater activation during interoceptive processing (BDT) than during exteroceptive processing (DDT), irrespective of the feedback type.
source: In specific, (1) the bilateral AIC demonstrated greater activation during interoceptive processing (BDT) than during exteroceptive processing (DDT), irrespective of the feedback type
evidence: This claim is supported by ROI analysis of AIC activation patterns shown in Figure 2d.

claim: The delayed trials induced greater activation in the bilateral AIC in comparison to the non-delayed trials only during interoceptive processing (BDT).
source: (2) the delayed trials induced greater activation in the bilateral AIC in comparison to the non-delayed trials only during interoceptive processing (BDT).
evidence: This claim is supported by ROI analysis of AIC activation patterns shown in Figure 2d.

claim: The interaction effect in the AIC suggests that the AIC was actively engaged in interoceptive processing.
source: The evidence of this interaction effect in the AIC suggests that the AIC was actively engaged in interoceptive processing.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the interaction effect observed in the fMRI data.

claim: Higher interoceptive accuracy was associated with greater interaction effect of the bilateral AIC (and MTG) across participants.
source: Voxel-wise regression analysis revealed the relationship between the interoceptive task-induced activation strength (map of the interaction contrast) and participants' interoceptive accuracy (performance accuracy in the BDT), with exteroceptive accuracy (performance accuracy in the DDT) controlled as a covariate. Higher interoceptive accuracy was associated with greater interaction effect of the bilateral AIC (and MTG) across participants (Figure 3a, Table 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by regression analysis results shown in Figure 3a and Table 6.

claim: AIC activation during interoceptive processing predicted individual differences in interoceptive attention.
source: The AIC activation during the interoceptive processing involved attending to physiological signals and matching bodily signals to external visual input, which predicted individual differences in interoceptive attention (see Figure 3b for the illustration).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 3b.

claim: PPI analysis showed augmented connectivity between the right AIC and the SMA/ACC, the FEF, the IFG, and the PoCG during interoceptive (versus exteroceptive) attention.
source: Psychophysiological interaction (PPI) analysis showed augmented connectivity between the right AIC (as the seed) and the SMA/ACC, the FEF, the inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), and the postcentral gyrus (PoCG) during interoceptive (versus exteroceptive) attention (BDT vs. DDT) in contrast to the reduced connectivity between the right AIC and visual cortices (VCs) modulated by interoceptive attention (Figure 4a, Table 7).
evidence: This claim is supported by PPI analysis results shown in Figure 4a and Table 7.

claim: PPI analysis showed reduced connectivity between the right AIC and visual cortices modulated by interoceptive attention.
source: Psychophysiological interaction (PPI) analysis showed augmented connectivity between the right AIC (as the seed) and the SMA/ACC, the FEF, the inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), and the postcentral gyrus (PoCG) during interoceptive (versus exteroceptive) attention (BDT vs. DDT) in contrast to the reduced connectivity between the right AIC and visual cortices (VCs) modulated by interoceptive attention (Figure 4a, Table 7).
evidence: This claim is supported by PPI analysis results shown in Figure 4a and Table 7.

claim: An increase in activation in the right AIC was associated with a greater increase in activation in the FEF, the IFG, and the PoCG under interoceptive attention compared with exteroceptive attention.
source: This result indicates that an increase in activation in the right AIC was associated with a greater increase in activation in the FEF, the IFG, and the PoCG and a greater decrease in activation in the VCs under interoceptive attention compared with exteroceptive attention (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the PPI results illustrated in Figure 4b.

claim: An increase in activation in the right AIC was associated with a greater decrease in activation in the VCs under interoceptive attention compared with exteroceptive attention.
source: This result indicates that an increase in activation in the right AIC was associated with a greater increase in activation in the FEF, the IFG, and the PoCG and a greater decrease in activation in the VCs under interoceptive attention compared with exteroceptive attention (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the PPI results illustrated in Figure 4b.

claim: The winning DCM model had an exceedance probability of 29.84% and included modulatory effects of interoceptive and exteroceptive attention on the connection from the AIC to the PoCG and from the AIC to V2/3.
source: For model comparison, random-effects (RFX) Bayesian model selection (BMS) indicated that the winning model (with an exceedance probability of 29.84%) was the one with the modulatory effects of interoceptive and exteroceptive attention (BDT and DDT) exerting on the connection from the AIC to the PoCG and from the AIC to V2/3 (Figure 4c and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by DCM model comparison results shown in Figure 4c and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The BMS indicated that interoceptive and exteroceptive attention were achieved through modulating the top-down connectivity from the AIC to the PoCG and V2/3 sensory cortices.
source: The BMS indicated that interoceptive and exteroceptive attention were achieved through modulating the top-down connectivity from the AIC to these two sensory cortices.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DCM model selection results.

source: t(8) = −2.35, p=0.009, BF = 3.95 compared with BDC)

claim: For the BDT, patients with AIC lesions had significantly lower discrimination sensitivity (dʹ) compared with NC (t(13) = −3.62, p<0.001, BF = 13.78).
source: and discrimination sensitivity (dʹ) compared with the NCs and BDCs groups (t(13) = −3.62, p<0.001, BF = 13.78 compared with NC
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical comparison of behavioral data from the lesion study.

claim: For the BDT, patients with AIC lesions had significantly lower discrimination sensitivity (dʹ) compared with BDC (t(8) = −2.22, p=0.013, BF = 3.40).
source: t(8) = −2.22, p=0.013, BF = 3.40 compared with BDC)
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical comparison of behavioral data from the lesion study.

claim: AIC lesion patients showed diminished interoceptive attention.
source: indicating diminished interoceptive attention
evidence: This is an interpretation of the behavioral deficits observed in AIC lesion patients.

claim: There was no significant difference in BDT accuracy between the NC and BDC groups (t(8) = 0, p=0.3).
source: However, we did not find significant difference in accuracy between the NC and BDC groups (t(8) = 0, p=0.3
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical comparison of behavioral data from the lesion study.

claim: There was no significant difference in BDT dʹ between the NC and BDC groups (t(8) = 0.112, p=0.23).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical comparison of behavioral data from the lesion study.

claim: For the DDT, patients with AIC lesions did not show significant abnormalities in performance accuracy compared with NC (t(9) = 0.18, p=0.22, BF = 0.38).
source: For the DDT, the patients with AIC lesions did not show significant abnormalities in performance accuracy (AIC vs. NC: t(9) = 0.18, p=0.22, BF = 0.38
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical comparison of behavioral data from the lesion study.

claim: For the DDT, patients with AIC lesions did not show significant abnormalities in performance accuracy compared with BDC (t(7) = −0.99, p=0.10, BF = 0.98).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical comparison of behavioral data from the lesion study.

claim: For the DDT, patients with AIC lesions did not show significant abnormalities in dʹ compared with NC (t(9) = 0.18, p=0.22, BF = 0.38).
source: and in dʹ (AIC vs. NC: t(9) = 0.18, p=0.22, BF = 0.38
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical comparison of behavioral data from the lesion study.

claim: For the DDT, patients with AIC lesions did not show significant abnormalities in dʹ compared with BDC (t(7) = −0.83, p=0.12, BF = 0.85).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical comparison of behavioral data from the lesion study.

claim: There was no significant interaction effect on β (F <1, p=0.65) in the lesion study.
source: We did not find significant interaction effect on β (F <1, p=0.65)
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of behavioral data from the lesion study.

claim: The lesion study results demonstrated significant impairment in discrimination ability when attending to bodily signals, but not to external visual input, in patients with AIC lesions.
source: Our results demonstrated significant impairment in discrimination ability when attending to bodily signals, but not to external visual input, in patients with AIC lesions.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the lesion study behavioral results.

claim: The AIC is critical for interoceptive attention to reach subjective awareness by integrating information from an individual's homeostatic state and the external environment.
source: Basing from previous evidence (e.g., Critchley, 2004), we hypothesized that the AIC is critical for interoceptive attention to reach subjective awareness by integrating information from an individual's homeostatic state and the external environment.
evidence: This is the main hypothesis of the study, supported by previous evidence and tested through the experiments.

claim: The insula is activated by autonomic arousal and emotional reactions.
source: Previous functional neuroimaging studies have shown that the insula is activated by autonomic arousal and emotional reactions (Craig, 2002; Craig, 2003; Critchley et al., 2004)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous neuroimaging studies.

claim: The achievement of interoceptive awareness depends on the integration of afferent bodily signals with higher-order contextual information attributable to the AIC.
source: The achievement of interoceptive awareness depends on the integration of afferent bodily signals with higher-order contextual information attributable to the AIC (Craig, 2002; Craig, 2009; Critchley, 2005; Damasio et al., 2000; Mutschler et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous theoretical and empirical work.

claim: The increase in neural activation in the AIC when focusing on breath rhythm indicates that the AIC supports attention toward bodily signals.
source: In this study, the increase in neural activation in the AIC and other related brain structures when focusing on breath rhythm indicates that the AIC supports attention toward bodily signals.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the fMRI activation results.

claim: The insula receives thalamo-insular projections of the interoceptive pathways.
source: Anatomically, the insula receives thalamo-insular projections of the interoceptive pathways (Craig, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to neuroanatomical literature.

claim: The AIC encodes subjective feelings.
source: The AIC encodes subjective feelings (Craig, 2003; Craig, 2009; Flynn, 1999)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The AIC is critical for instantaneous representation of the state of the body.
source: and is critical for instantaneous representation of the state of the body (Allen et al., 2016; Allen and Friston, 2018; Cao et al., 2014; Gu et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: During the BDT, interoceptive processing is achieved by attending to bodily signals (breath rhythm) and matching them to external visual feedback (the breath curve).
source: During the BDT, this is achieved by attending to bodily signals (i.e., breath rhythm) and matching them to external visual feedback (i.e., the breath curve).
evidence: This is a description of the cognitive processes involved in the BDT task.

claim: The activation of the right AIC is related to accuracy in sensing the timing of one's bodily signals, for example, heartbeat.
source: The present results provide additional support to previous finding that the activation of the right AIC is related to accuracy in sensing the timing of one's bodily signals, for example, heartbeat (Critchley et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim connects the current findings to previous research through citation.

claim: The insula works as a hub to convey bodily information into internal feelings for maintaining homeostasis.
source: Consistent with the notion that the AIC contributes to accurate perception of bodily states (Bechara and Naqvi, 2004), the insula works as a hub to convey bodily information into internal feelings for maintaining homeostasis and to mediate the representations of visceral states that link to the representations of the external world (Farb et al., 2013a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous theoretical work.

claim: The insula mediates the representations of visceral states that link to the representations of the external world.
source: Consistent with the notion that the AIC contributes to accurate perception of bodily states (Bechara and Naqvi, 2004), the insula works as a hub to convey bodily information into internal feelings for maintaining homeostasis and to mediate the representations of visceral states that link to the representations of the external world (Farb et al., 2013a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous theoretical work.

claim: The brain actively tries to predict possible future states and to minimize the difference between actual and predicted states according to predictive coding.
source: Our finding of a critical role of the AIC in interoceptive attention fits with a recent predictive coding account of the brain (Bastos et al., 2012; Friston and Kiebel, 2009; Rao and Ballard, 1999), which suggests that the brain actively tries to predict possible future states and to minimize the difference between actual and predicted states.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to predictive coding literature.

claim: Interoceptive predictions are computed within a network of brain regions with the AIC as the key node.
source: In the context of interoceptive and embodied predictive coding (Allen and Friston, 2018; Gu et al., 2013), previous studies hypothesized that interoceptive predictions are computed within a network of brain regions with the AIC as the key node (Allen et al., 2016; Barrett and Simmons, 2015; Seth, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous theoretical work on predictive coding.

claim: The AIC is the only region that shows a reciprocal increase in connectivity with the somatosensory cortex in a tactile oddball paradigm.
source: One such study using a tactile oddball paradigm and DCM of fMRI time series demonstrated that the AIC is the only region, among a network of body-related brain regions, that shows a reciprocal increase in connectivity with the somatosensory cortex (Allen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous DCM study.

claim: The current finding extends the role of the AIC in predictive coding to breathing-related interoception.
source: Our finding is consistent with this previous study and extends the role of the AIC in predictive coding to breathing-related interoception by using both fMRI and lesion approaches.
evidence: This is a statement about the contribution of the current study relative to previous work.

claim: Relative to non-insular lesion patients and healthy controls, AIC lesions led to a deficit in accuracy and sensitivity of interoceptive attention.
source: Relative to non-insular lesion patients and healthy controls, AIC lesions led to a deficit in accuracy and sensitivity of interoceptive attention.
evidence: This is a summary of the lesion study findings.

claim: The findings from the lesion study provide causal evidence demonstrating the critical role of the AIC in interoceptive attention.
source: These findings provide causal evidence demonstrating the critical role of the AIC in interoceptive attention.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the lesion study results emphasizing their causal nature.

claim: The insular cortex is considered as a limbic sensory region that participates in the intuitive processing of complex situations.
source: Traditionally, the insular cortex is considered as a limbic sensory region that participates in the intuitive processing of complex situations (Augustine, 1996; Butti and Hof, 2010; Menon and Uddin, 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The insular cortex integrates ascending visceromotor and somatosensory inputs with attention systems via intrinsic connectivity to identify and respond to salient stimuli.
source: by integrating the ascending visceromotor and somatosensory inputs with attention systems via intrinsic connectivity to identify and respond to salient stimuli (Menon and Uddin, 2010; Uddin, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The AIC is a node that mediates cognitive processes including bottom-up control of attention.
source: The AIC, in particular, is a node that mediates cognitive processes including bottom-up control of attention (Corbetta et al., 2002; Corbetta et al., 2008; Wu et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The AIC mediates conscious detection of signals arising from the autonomic nervous system.
source: and conscious detection of signals arising from the autonomic nervous system (Craig, 2002; Critchley, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The behavioral deficit of interoceptive attention in patients with AIC lesions is due to the disruption in the integration of the somatic and visceral inputs with the abstract representation of the present internal state.
source: Therefore, the behavioral deficit of interoceptive attention in patients with AIC lesions is due to the disruption in the integration of the somatic and visceral inputs with the abstract representation of the present internal state (i.e., the saliency of a certain type of signals).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mechanism underlying the behavioral deficits in AIC lesion patients.

claim: Disruption in integration of somatic and visceral inputs with abstract representation leads to failure in discriminating whether the displayed respiratory curve is different from internal states.
source: Consequently, it leads to failure in discriminating whether the displayed respiratory curve is different from internal states.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mechanism underlying the behavioral deficits in AIC lesion patients.

claim: Most previous lesion studies indicated interoceptive deficits with AIC lesions.
source: Most previous lesion studies indicated interoceptive deficits with AIC lesions (Critchley and Garfinkel, 2017; García-Cordero et al., 2016; Ibañez et al., 2010; Ronchi et al., 2015; Starr et al., 2009; Terasawa et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple previous lesion studies.

claim: Interoceptive accuracy relies on a widely distributed network with the insular cortex as a key node.
source: supporting the conclusion that interoceptive accuracy relies on a widely distributed network with the insular cortex as a key node (Craig, 2002; Critchley and Harrison, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Preservation of interoceptive processing was documented in one patient with bilateral insular damages.
source: However, the preservations of interoceptive processing (Khalsa et al., 2009) and self-awareness across a large battery of tests (Philippi et al., 2012) were documented in one patient with bilateral insular damages.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to case studies.

claim: Self-awareness was preserved across a large battery of tests in one patient with bilateral insular damages.
source: However, the preservations of interoceptive processing (Khalsa et al., 2009) and self-awareness across a large battery of tests (Philippi et al., 2012) were documented in one patient with bilateral insular damages.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to case studies.

claim: Interoceptive processing based on subjective report focusing on 'feeling/awareness' might be compensated by other brain structures such as the brainstem and subcortical structures.
source: These studies are mostly based on subjective report focusing on 'feeling/awareness' (Khalsa et al., 2009) that might be compensated by other brain structures such as the brainstem and subcortical structures, for example, nucleus tractus solitaries, the parabrachial nucleus, area postrema and hypothalamus (Damasio et al., 2013), frontal and temporal regions, for example, amygdala, superior temporal gyrus, and temporal pole (García-Cordero et al., 2016; Shany-Ur et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: The BDT challenged interoceptive attention that requires the integration of interoceptive awareness and accuracy.
source: In the current study, the BDT challenged interoceptive attention that requires the integration of interoceptive awareness and accuracy.
evidence: This is a description of the task demands of the BDT.

claim: Lesions of the AIC were associated with a deficit in performance on the interoceptive task, indicating that the AIC is critical in supporting the precision of interoceptive processing.
source: Our examination of interoceptive attention in patients with focal AIC lesions showed that lesions of the AIC were associated with a deficit in performance, indicating that the AIC is critical in supporting the precision of interoceptive processing.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the lesion study findings.

claim: Interoceptive attention is the mechanism that coordinates the processing of bodily signals and higher-level representation of that information.
source: Interoceptive attention is the mechanism that coordinates the processing of bodily signals and higher-level representation of that information.
evidence: This is a conceptual definition of interoceptive attention.

claim: The AIC encodes and represents bodily information and transmits this information to other neural systems for advanced computations in conscious perception and decision-making.
source: The AIC reportedly encodes and represents bodily information (e.g., visceral states) and transmits this information to other neural systems for advanced computations in conscious perception and decision-making (Bechara and Naqvi, 2004; Flynn, 1999; Gu and FitzGerald, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The AIC is a key node of the large-scale network that detects information from multiple sources and generates subjective awareness.
source: The AIC is a key node of the large-scale network that detects information from multiple sources including objective visceral signals, generates subjective awareness (Craig, 2009; Gu et al., 2012; Gu et al., 2015; Kleckner et al., 2017; Seeley et al., 2007)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The AIC responds to the switch between networks that supports internal oriented processing and cognitive control.
source: and responds to the switch between networks that supports internal oriented processing and cognitive control (Menon, 2011; Menon and Uddin, 2010; Sridharan et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The AIC is intrinsically connected to the somatosensory area of the PoCG and this connection is positively modulated by interoceptive attention.
source: Supporting this argument, we showed that the AIC is intrinsically connected to the somatosensory area of the PoCG and that this connection is positively modulated by interoceptive attention (relative to exteroceptive attention).
evidence: This claim is supported by DCM analysis results.

claim: Higher-level areas including the ACC/SMA, FEF, and IFG of the cognitive control network are involved in the interoceptive process.
source: Other higher-level areas, for example, the ACC/SMA, FEF, and IFG of the so-called cognitive control network (CCN) (Fan, 2014; Wu et al., 2018), are also involved in the interoceptive process.
evidence: This claim is supported by fMRI activation and connectivity results.

claim: Both somatosensory afferents and a network that includes the AIC and the ACC are possible pathways of interoceptive attention.
source: Both somatosensory afferents and a network that includes the AIC and the ACC are possible pathways of interoceptive attention (Khalsa et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The AIC may play a central role in integrating sensory signals from the PoCG and visual cortex and sends top-down signals that guide sensation and perception.
source: The AIC may play a central role in integrating sensory signals from the PoCG and visual cortex and sends top-down signals that guide sensation and perception through a dynamic interaction with sensory or bottom-up information.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the connectivity results.

claim: Somatosensory information concerning the internal state of the body is conveyed through the PoCG.
source: Somatosensory information concerning the internal state of the body is conveyed through the PoCG, as well as the visual signals in V2/3 containing the majority of external information.
evidence: This is a statement based on neuroanatomical knowledge.

claim: Visual signals in V2/3 contain the majority of external information.
source: Somatosensory information concerning the internal state of the body is conveyed through the PoCG, as well as the visual signals in V2/3 containing the majority of external information.
evidence: This is a statement based on neuroanatomical knowledge.

claim: The top-down modulation of the AIC in interoceptive attention is accomplished by augmenting the efferent signals to the somatosensory cortices.
source: The top-down modulation of the AIC in interoceptive attention is accomplished by augmenting the efferent signals to the somatosensory cortices.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DCM results.

claim: A first-order mapping of internal feeling is supported by insular and somatosensory cortices.
source: This result is consistent with the argument that a first-order mapping of internal feeling is supported by insular and somatosensory cortices (Damasio, 2003)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous theoretical work.

claim: Somatosensory information critically contributes to interoceptive attention.
source: and that somatosensory information critically contributes to interoceptive attention (Khalsa et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In the BDT, interoceptive attention reflects a combination of attention to the internal bodily signal (the breath) and the external visual stimulus (the curve).
source: In the BDT, interoceptive attention reflects a combination of the attention to the internal bodily signal (i.e., the breath) and the external visual stimulus (i.e., the curve).
evidence: This is a description of the task demands of the BDT.

claim: The AIC may distribute and balance the processes of external and internal information to coordinate perceptual processing.
source: To coordinate perceptual processing, the AIC may distribute and balance the processes of external and internal information.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the AIC's role based on the study findings.

claim: The winning DCM model and parameter inference provide evidence that interoceptive attention is achieved mainly by modulating the connectivity between the AIC and the somatosensory areas (PoCG).
source: The winning model and parameter inference from DCM provide evidence that interoceptive attention is achieved mainly by modulating the connectivity between the AIC and the somatosensory areas (PoCG)
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DCM results.

claim: Exteroceptive attention is primarily modulated via the connectivity between the AIC and V2/3.
source: while exteroceptive attention is primarily modulated via the connectivity between the AIC and V2/3.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DCM results.

claim: The dynamic adjustment of the connectivity of the AIC to sensory cortices is the foundation of interoceptive attention for bodily signals and of exteroceptive attention for external objects or inputs.
source: We propose that the dynamic adjustment of the connectivity of the AIC to sensory cortices is the foundation of interoceptive attention for bodily signals, which is critical for homeostatic regulation, and of exteroceptive attention for external objects or inputs.
evidence: This is a theoretical proposal based on the study findings.

claim: The error rate arising from the difficulty in heartbeat counting or non-sensory process confounds are inherent to cardioception designs.
source: Although the neural correlates of interoceptive awareness have been studied by other tasks, such as the heartbeat detection task (Bechara and Naqvi, 2004; Critchley et al., 2004; Khalsa et al., 2009; Ring et al., 2015), the error rate arising from the difficulty in heartbeat counting or non-sensory process confounds are inherent to these cardioception designs (Kleckner et al., 2015; Ring et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to methodological critiques of heartbeat tasks.

claim: Breath can be clearly perceived and autonomously controlled, in contrast to cardioception.
source: In contrast to cardioception, breath can be clearly perceived and autonomously controlled.
evidence: This is a statement based on physiological knowledge.

claim: The feature that breath can be clearly perceived and autonomously controlled enabled the design of a task measuring interoceptive attention.
source: This feature enabled us to design a task measuring interoceptive attention, which requires that the target of interoception be clearly and vividly perceivable by our consciousness.
evidence: This is a methodological rationale for the task design.

claim: The positive correlations between objective interoceptive accuracy during the BDT and subjectively scored difficulty of interoceptive task relative to exteroceptive task demonstrates that the BDT is valid in assessing interoceptive attention.
source: The positive correlations between objective interoceptive accuracy during the BDT and subjectively scored difficulty of interoceptive task relative to exteroceptive task (i.e., interoceptive awareness) further demonstrates that the BDT is valid in assessing interoceptive attention.
evidence: This is a validation argument based on correlation analysis.

claim: The respiratory interoception task is a non-intrusive measurement with low cognitive load that is more practical for patients with focal brain damage than demanding cardiac interoception tasks.
source: We developed the respiratory interoception task as a non-intrusive measurement with low cognitive load that is more practical for patients with focal brain damage than the demanding cardiac interoception tasks.
evidence: This is a statement about the methodological advantages of the BDT.

claim: The BDT may not represent a pure probe of interoception because respiratory processes can also be tracked using exteroceptive and proprioceptive information.
source: The BDT may not represent a pure probe of interoception because respiratory processes can also be tracked using exteroceptive and proprioceptive information.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a potential limitation of the task.

claim: The cognitive subtraction of DDT from BDT leaves the interoceptive and proprioceptive processing components of interoception.
source: In our design, we included the DDT for a measure of exteroception so that the cognitive subtraction of DDT from BDT leaves the interoceptive and proprioceptive processing components of interoception (Gu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a methodological rationale for the task design.

claim: The delayed duration in the BDT was fixed to 400 ms, approximately 1/10 of an average cycle of normal healthy people (3–4 s/cycle).
source: In the BDT, the delayed manipulation in our study was fixed to 400 ms, approximately 1/10 of an average cycle of normal healthy people (i.e., 3–4 s/cycle).
evidence: This is a description of the task parameters.

claim: The delayed duration can be manipulated according to each individual's respiratory cycle to control subjective task difficulty across participants.
source: This delayed duration can be manipulated according to each individual's respiratory cycle in an effort to control subjective task difficulty across participants.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future methodological refinement.

claim: Attention can be categorized into interoceptive attention, exteroceptive attention, and executive control of attention depending on the source of information.
source: Depending on the source of information, attention can be categorized into (1) interoceptive attention, which is directed toward bodily signals such as somatic and visceral signals (e.g., in a heartbeat detection or counting task); (2) exteroceptive attention, which is directed toward primary sensory inputs from outside (e.g., visual and auditory stimuli); and (3) executive control of attention, which coordinates thoughts and actions (e.g., in Color Stroop, flanker, and working memory tasks; see review Fan, 2014).
evidence: This is a conceptual framework for categorizing attention types.

claim: Extensive studies have focused on the attentional modulation of sensory and perceptual inputs and on the executive control of attention.
source: Although extensive studies have focused on the attentional modulation of sensory and perceptual inputs and on the executive control of attention, interoceptive attention is difficult to study because the vast majority of intrinsic visceral activity, except breath effort, cannot be clearly perceived under normal conditions.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the literature.

claim: Interoceptive attention is difficult to study because the vast majority of intrinsic visceral activity, except breath effort, cannot be clearly perceived under normal conditions.
source: Although extensive studies have focused on the attentional modulation of sensory and perceptual inputs and on the executive control of attention, interoceptive attention is difficult to study because the vast majority of intrinsic visceral activity, except breath effort, cannot be clearly perceived under normal conditions.
evidence: This is a statement about methodological challenges in studying interoceptive attention.

claim: Using the BDT to examine attentional deployment toward breath effort enabled the revelation of the neural mechanism of interoceptive attention.
source: Using the BDT to examine attentional deployment toward breath effort enabled us to reveal the neural mechanism of interoceptive attention.
evidence: This is a statement about the methodological contribution of the study.

claim: The perceptible, controllable, measurable, and autonomous features of breathing guaranteed more accurate and reliable measurement of individual differences in interoceptive ability.
source: In general, the perceptible, controllable, measurable, and autonomous features of breathing guaranteed more accurate and reliable measurement of individual differences in interoceptive ability.
evidence: This is a statement about the methodological advantages of using breathing for interoceptive tasks.

claim: Breath plays a potentially important role in generating and regulating emotion as a type of interoceptive attention that could be clearly perceived and autonomously controlled.
source: As a type of interoceptive attention that could be clearly perceived and autonomously controlled, breath plays a potentially important role in generating and regulating emotion.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the broader implications of breath-related interoceptive attention.

claim: Mindfulness meditation can be viewed as a practice involving interoceptive attention.
source: For example, mindfulness meditation, which is now well known for its role in emotion regulation and mental health (Khoury et al., 2015), can be viewed as a practice involving interoceptive attention.
evidence: This is a conceptual interpretation supported by a citation.

claim: One primary method of mindfulness meditation is to bring one's attention and awareness to the current experiences of the movement of the abdomen when breathing or the breath as it enters and exits the nostrils.
source: One of its primary methods is to bring one's attention (the processing) and then awareness (the outcome) to the current experiences of the movement of the abdomen when breathing in and out or the breath as it enters and exits the nostrils.
evidence: This is a description of meditation practice based on general knowledge.

claim: The AIC plays an important role in meditation based on the revealed neural mechanisms of interoceptive attention.
source: Considering the revealed neural mechanisms of interoceptive attention in this study, we predict that the AIC plays an important role in meditation.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the study findings.

claim: Meditation experience is associated with increased gray matter thickness in the AIC.
source: Findings that meditation experience is associated with increased gray matter thickness in the AIC (Lazar et al., 2005)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous neuroimaging study.

claim: Meditation experience is associated with increased gyrification (increase in folding) of the AIC.
source: and increased gyrification (increase in folding) of the AIC (Luders et al., 2012) support this prediction.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous neuroimaging study.

claim: Meditation training may enhance interoceptive attention to focus on bodily signals so that accurate feelings can be generated based on bodily responses.
source: Meditation training may enhance interoceptive attention to focus on bodily signals so that accurate feelings can be generated based on the bodily responses
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the potential effects of meditation.

claim: Meditation may release the mind from intensive involvement of exteroceptive and executive control of attention that consumes the majority of mental resources.
source: meanwhile the mind can be released from an intensive involvement of exteroceptive and executive control of attention (the internal attention for the coordination of thought processing) that consumes the majority of mental resources.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the potential effects of meditation.

claim: The implementation of the interoceptive task extends the research on interoceptive processing into the respiratory domain with demonstrated validity and reliability.
source: In addition, the implementation of the interoceptive task extends the research on interoceptive processing into the respiratory domain with the validity and reliability demonstrated.
evidence: This is a statement about the methodological contribution of the study.

claim: The interoceptive task may have significant applications in studying issues related to interoceptive attention in patients with neuropsychiatric disorders, such as anxiety and autism.
source: It may have significant applications in studying issues related to interoceptive attention in patients with neuropsychiatric disorders, such as anxiety (Avery et al., 2014) and autism (Barrett and Simmons, 2015; Quattrocki and Friston, 2014)
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications supported by citations.

claim: The interoceptive task may have significant applications in studying issues related to interoceptive attention in patients with substance use disorders.
source: and in patients with substance use disorders (Sönmez et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications supported by a citation.

claim: A respiratory transducer fastened around the participants' upper chest was utilized to record breathing effort by measuring thoracic changes in circumference during respiration.
source: A respiratory transducer (TSD201, MRI compatible, BIOPAC Systems Inc), which was fastened around the participants' upper chest, was utilized to record breathing effort by measuring thoracic changes in circumference during respiration.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental apparatus.

claim: The signal for the change in circumference was sampled at 1000 Hz using the BIOPAC MP150/RSP100C system.
source: The signal for the change in circumference was sampled at 1000 Hz using the BIOPAC MP150/RSP100C system, passing through a DC amplifier with low-pass filtering at 1 Hz and high-pass filtering at 0.05 Hz, and gain set to 10 V.
evidence: This is a description of the data acquisition parameters.

claim: The first fMRI sample included 44 adults (23 females and 21 males, mean age 21.43 ± 2.51 years, age range: 19–29 years).
source: The fMRI experiments included two samples of participants: the first sample included 44 adults (23 females and 21 males, mean age ± standard deviation: 21.43 ± 2.51 years, age range: 19–29 years)
evidence: This is a description of the participant sample.

claim: The second fMRI sample included 28 adults (14 females and 14 males, mean age 21.93 ± 2.11 years, age range: 18–26 years).
source: and the second sample included additional 28 adults (14 females and 14 males, mean age ± standard deviation: 21.93 ± 2.11 years, age range: 18–26 years).
evidence: This is a description of the participant sample.

claim: All participants in the fMRI studies were right-handed (except for one participant).
source: All participants were right-handed (except for one participant)
evidence: This is a description of participant characteristics.

claim: Six male patients (33–53 years old, mean 42.17 ± SD 7.31 years) with focal unilateral insular cortex lesions participated in the lesion study.
source: Six male patients (33–53 years old, mean 42.17 ± SD 7.31 years) with focal unilateral insular cortex lesions participated in the lesion study (see Table 9 for patient characteristics).
evidence: This is a description of the patient sample.
